newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says orphanages used in child-sex trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says orphanages used in child-sex trade.

text.p: Sri Lankan human rights groups on Sunday said orphanages in the country were being used to supply children to foreign paedophiles.

"One of the main ways foreign paedophiles sexually abuse children in Sri Lanka is through orphanages and homes for children," said Maureen Seneviratne of Protecting Environment and Children Everywhere (PEACE), an outfit trying to raise awareness about the evils of child-sex tourism.
Human rights groups have said Sri Lanka, which relies on tourism as a major source of foreign exchange and employment, has become a popular destination for the world's paedophiles in recent years.
Police are probing the activities of a Belgian tour operator suspected of running an orphanage that hired out children to foreign paedophiles, children's rights campaigners and police said on Sunday.
"We've asked police to investigate a Belgian tour operator alleged to be running an unregistered children's home," Sugath Ranugge, commissioner of Child Care Services, told Reuters.
Police said children from the orphanage, near the tourist resort of Sigiriya, 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Colombo, were alleged to have been taken to nearby hotels for sex with foreigners.
The Belgian tour operator also had opened another orphanage near Colombo recently, they said.
Last year, Sri Lanka passed new laws aimed at discouraging foreign paedophiles and put police on alert against child prostitution.
The law calls for a minimum five-year jail term and a maximum 20-year sentence for pimps and their clients.
Seneviratne of PEACE said authorities had not been alert enough and the laws was not being enforced, allowing paedophiles to abuse thousands of children.

"Our campaign is flooded with information on safe houses and connections between orphanages and paedophiles rings," she told Reuters. "We have come across homes like this all over the country. We do not have open sex tourism like in Bangkok or the Philippines."
"Thousands of children are being abused," she added. "We have on many occasions told immigration authorities not to give visas to suspected paedophiles but they keep coming."
Most of the children abused by paedophiles were either beachcombers, street children or orphans, she said.
Many paedophiles operating in the island were rich and had influential connections, she said.
Police said a Swiss national, another Belgian and a German were currently awaiting trial on child-sex charges. A second Swiss man fled the country while on bail after being charged with paedophilia.

Police Deputy Inspector-General Mohamed Nizam, head of the police department's Child Desk, said police were probing possible links between foreign paedophiles in Sri Lanka and the child-sex gang in Belgium which abducted, abused and -- in at least four cases -- murdered children.
